Cut text to a token count, keeping the part you choose

Source: R/core-context-policy.R
hr_truncate.Rd

keep = "head" (the default) keeps the start of text and is gr_truncate_tokens() itself, so a caller that switches to this function sends what it sent before. "tail" keeps the end, with marker at the front. "both" keeps the start and the end, about half the budget each, with marker between them on a line of its own. "scored" splits the text into units (the elements of text when it has more than one, else its paragraphs, split at blank lines), keeps the units with the highest scores that fit, and joins them with a blank line in their original order, followed by marker when any unit was dropped; when no unit fits beside the marker, the units that fit without it are kept with no marker. With marker = "", "tail" and "both" have the whole budget for text, as "head" does; "both" keeps only the start when the end has no room, and only the end when no word of the start fits. The result is never longer than n tokens.

Usage

hr_truncate(
  text,
  n,
  keep = c("head", "tail", "both", "scored"),
  scores = NULL,
  marker = " ...[truncated]",
  trace = NULL,
  where = "truncate",
  piece = NULL
)

Arguments

text

A single string; for keep = "scored", a character vector of units is accepted as well.

n

Maximum token count.

keep

"head", "tail", "both" or "scored".

scores

For keep = "scored": one number per unit, higher kept first. Ties keep the earlier unit.

marker

The text that marks a cut; "" for none. As in gr_truncate_tokens(), it is dropped when it would cost half the budget or more.

trace

Optional gr_trace to write the cut to.

where

The cut site, written to the trace, in the dotted style of call labels ("refine.draft").

piece

The name of the piece that was cut, written to the trace, or NULL.

Value

A single string.

Details

With a trace, a cut writes a "truncate" step that records where, piece, keep, dropped_part ("end", "start", "middle", or the units dropped, as "units 2, 5"), the token counts before and after and tokens_dropped. Nothing is written when the text fits.

See also

hr_context_policy(), hr_context_fit(), gr_truncate_tokens()

Other cost and token functions: gr_budget(), gr_count_tokens(), gr_estimate_cost(), gr_model_info(), gr_model_limits(), gr_models(), gr_register_model(), gr_set_tokenizer(), gr_tokenizer(), gr_truncate_tokens(), hr_context_fit(), hr_context_policy()

Examples

txt <- paste("Para", 1:6, "says something about revenue.", collapse = "\n\n")
hr_truncate(txt, 20)                      # the start, as gr_truncate_tokens()
#> [1] "Para 1 says something about revenue. ...[truncated]"
hr_truncate(txt, 20, keep = "tail")       # the end
#> [1] "...[truncated] Para 6 says something about revenue."
cat(hr_truncate(txt, 24, keep = "both"))  # both ends
#> Para 1 says
#> ...[truncated]
#> something about revenue.
# The paragraphs that score highest, in document order.
cat(hr_truncate(txt, 20, keep = "scored", scores = c(1, 9, 2, 8, 3, 4)))
#> Para 2 says something about revenue.
#> 
#> ...[truncated]

# The cut is written to a trace.
tr <- gr_trace()
invisible(hr_truncate(txt, 20, keep = "tail", trace = tr, where = "demo", piece = "notes"))
tr$steps[[1]]$detail[c("where", "piece", "dropped_part", "tokens_dropped")]
#> $where
#> [1] "demo"
#> 
#> $piece
#> [1] "notes"
#> 
#> $dropped_part
#> [1] "start"
#> 
#> $tokens_dropped
#> [1] 43
#>
